title: Enterprise Onboarding — Integration, Escalation, Known Issues & QBR Playbook
author: Priya Desai
content:
Overview:
This playbook consolidates the canonical process and artifacts Customer Success (CS), Support, and SRE use for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference. It covers the onboarding checklist, integration guidance, the escalation playbook, a curated known-issues & workarounds list, and the material we present during health checks and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It is intended for CS Leads, Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, SREs, and customer engineering teams.

Scope:
- Applies to customers contracting Dedicated or Private deployments and strategic Hosted customers with enterprise SLAs.
- Covers pre-production integration through first 90 days of production and recurring QBR cadence.

Goals:
- Ensure predictable, repeatable onboarding that meets SLA and performance targets.
- Reduce time-to-first-successful-call and mean time to resolution (MTTR) for customer-facing incidents.
- Provide standardized QBR materials and success metrics to drive retention and expansion.

Ownership and Roles:
- CS Lead (primary owner): manages relationship, schedules QBRs, owns health metrics (example: Alex Morgan).
- Solutions Engineer (integration owner): leads API/model integration and validation (example: Priya Desai).
- SRE on-call: owns platform incidents and escalation to infra/serving runtime (example: Daniel Kim).
- Customer Engineering Contact: customer-side technical owner.
- Exec sponsor (optional): executive-level relationship owner for major customers.

Onboarding Checklist (90-day runbook):
1) Kickoff (Day 0–3)
   - Introductions, success criteria, data classification, compliance constraints.
   - Deliverables: signed tech contacts, access matrix, initial runbook links.
2) Access & Networking (Day 1–7)
   - Validate IP allowlists, VPC peering (if Private), KMS/HSM key exchange.
   - Verify DNS routing, certificate exchange (TLS), and egress rules.
3) Authentication & Authorization (Day 2–10)
   - Issue API keys or service principals; confirm RBAC roles for team members.
4) Model Selection & Config (Day 3–14)
   - Agree on model variant (latency vs. quality), token limits, quantization profile.
   - Configure batching, KV cache TTL, and routing policy.
5) Integration Validation (Day 7–21)
   - Run integration test suite: smoke generation, streaming, embeddings, function calls.
   - Validate response schemas, streaming termination, and rate limiting behavior.
6) Performance Verification (Day 14–30)
   - Baseline P95 token latency, throughput, error rate under expected traffic.
   - Target SLOs: availability >= 99.9%, error rate < 0.5%, P95 latency <= 350ms (hosted), adjust for Dedicated based on agreed profile.
7) Security & Compliance Review (Day 14–30)
   - Confirm audit logging, data residency, retention policies, and SOC/ISO evidence as required.
8) Production Cutover (Day 30–60)
   - Canary rollout, monitoring of success metrics, automatic fallback rules engaged.
9) 30/60/90-day Health Checks
   - Operational review, cost/performance tuning, and any model quality regressions.

Integration Guide (summary):
- API endpoints: Use /v1/generate for text, /v1/embeddings for vectors. Follow SDK quickstarts in eng-developer-experience docs.
- Recommended client configuration:
  - Retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter, initial delay 100ms, max 10s, max attempts 5.
  - Timeouts: 30s for sync generation calls; 120s for long-running jobs or streaming.
  - Rate limits: respect X-RateLimit-* headers returned by the platform.

Sample config snippet (JSON):
{
  "model": "redwood-2-large",
  "max_tokens": 1024,
  "stream": true,
  "batching": {
    "enabled": true,
    "max_batch_size": 32
  }
}

Escalation Playbook (operational steps):
- Severity definitions:
  - S1 (Critical): Platform down for customer, data loss, or model unavailability preventing production use. Response target: 15 minutes.
  - S2 (High): Significant degradation (e.g., P95 latency > 2x target, high error rate) affecting >30% traffic. Response target: 1 hour.
  - S3 (Medium): Functional issue with workarounds; impacts limited feature set. Response target: 4 business hours.
  - S4 (Low): Cosmetic or non-urgent feature requests. Response target: next business day.

Escalation path (S1 example):
1) Customer reports via Support portal or opens SEV1 via CS Lead.
2) CS Lead triggers SRE on-call via PagerDuty and posts in #cs-oncall and #sre-incident with incident brief.
3) SRE runs immediate triage: check serving runtime, GPU pool health, autoscaler, and recent deploys.
4) If code-level root cause suspected, SRE escalates to Eng Serving Runtime on-call and creates an incident ticket.
5) CS Lead communicates status to customer at 15-minute cadence until full mitigation.
6) Post-incident: owner creates postmortem within 72 hours and assigns action items.

Escalation contacts & channels (role-based):
- Support portal: support.redwood.ai (preferred for ticketing).
- Slack channels: #cs-oncall, #sre-incident, #eng-serving-runtime.
- PagerDuty: on-call schedule (SRE and runtime teams).
- Executive escalation: CS Director -> VP of Customer Success -> CTO (if unresolved after 8 hours for S1).

Known Issues & Workarounds (selection):
- RI-2026-03: Intermittent streaming termination for large token windows
  - Symptom: Client receives final chunk prematurely for very large completions (>25k tokens).
  - Workaround: Reduce max_tokens per call and enable prefix KV caching for long contexts. Patch scheduled in runtime-release 2026.10.
- RI-2026-07: Embedding API occasional higher latency in eu-central-1
  - Symptom: P95 embedding latency spikes to 800–1200ms.
  - Workaround: Route embeddings to eu-west-1 or use dedicated capacity. Monitoring alert configured to auto-notify CS.
- RI-2026-11: Auth token TTL mismatch after key rotation
  - Symptom: Some service principals get 401 until token refresh window completes (5–10 minutes).
  - Workaround: Trigger manual token refresh or reissue keys; follow key-rotation checklist in eng-infra docs.

Support Process & SLAs:
- Ticket intake:
  - Preferred: Support portal (auto-triage) or CS ticket created by CS Lead.
  - Urgent: Open a SEV via PagerDuty and notify CS Lead.
- SLA commitments (Enterprise):
  - S1: Initial response within 15 minutes, collaborative mitigation until resolved.
  - S2: Initial response within 1 hour, continuous updates until mitigated.
  - S3: Initial response within 4 business hours.
  - S4: Response within 24 business hours.
- Escalation rules: change severity if customer production traffic impact changes; escalate to Eng at SRE discretion.

Health Checks & QBR Materials (what to present):
- Recommended metrics to present in health checks and QBRs:
  - Availability (monthly) and rolling 30-day window.
  - Token throughput (tokens/sec) and cost per 1M tokens.
  - Latency: P50, P95, P99 for inference and embeddings.
  - Error rates: 4xx vs 5xx breakdown.
  - Model quality metrics: BLEU/ROUGE-equivalents where applicable, user-reported regressions, eval set pass rate.
  - Cost optimization opportunities: batching savings, quantization recommendations, and routing policies.
- Dashboards and data sources:
  - Platform: eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts (Per-customer dashboards).
  - Logs: audit-logging (security); request traces available via tracing hooks.
  - Cost: billing reports (per-route breakdown) and token-level cost export.
- QBR agenda template:
  1) Attendees & Goals
  2) Last quarter summary: availability, incidents, and action items status
  3) Performance review: latency, throughput, error rate, and cost trends
  4) Model quality & evaluation summary
  5) Roadmap & upcoming platform changes affecting customer
  6) Action items and next steps (owners and due dates)

Templates & Artifacts to Attach to QBR:
- 30/60/90-day onboarding checklist (completed items and owners).
- Incident summaries and recent postmortems.
- Cost optimization proposals with expected delta in $/token.
- Runbook exports and alerting thresholds.

Continuous Improvement:
- After each onboarding and significant incident, CS and SRE conduct a retrospective and capture three concrete action items.
- Maintain a living regression test set (prompt-set-and-benchmarks) for each enterprise customer to detect model quality regressions before rollouts.

Document maintenance:
- Owner: Priya Desai (Solutions Engineering).
- Review cadence: quarterly; update after any major runtime release or process change.

If anything in this playbook conflicts with a customer's contract (SLA or security requirements), follow the contract and raise an exception with Legal and Security immediately.
